assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: The company's own FY2026 projection is the anchor: 2,840,000 tonnes of production and sales [S2 p.89, F15], down from 3.634 Mt realised in FY2025 (F3) as management cut output to focus on lower-cost pits and defend margin through a weak price year [S2 p.88]. That plan is already running: production for the six months to 30 June 2026 was 1.370 Mt [S4 p.15, F18], a 2.74 Mt annualised rate, so the 2.84 Mt full-year number is evidenced rather than aspirational. We hold the company's plan flat across the window: the record shows no sourced growth plan, the stated 2026 strategy is explicitly stability rather than aggressive expansion [S2 p.88], and the house card forbids an unsourced volume drift either way. The 137.9 Mt reserve supports this rate many times over, so volume, not depletion, is the constraint. The 18% below-plan realisation in 2025 (3.634 Mt against a 4.8 Mt target, F3) is why we do not reload to the historical 5-6 Mt capacity: management chose lower volume for margin, and no disclosure commits it to reversing that.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: CALIBRATED ON THE LAST TWO ACTUALS, not on a forecast-year spike. FY2025A realised price was US$41.33/t (F8; coal revenue US$150.2m over 3.634 Mt gives the same US$41.3) against a coal deck FY2025A Newcastle average of US$108.4/t, a ratio of 0.38; FY2024A was US$52.24/t (F7) against Newcastle US$136.1/t, a ratio of 0.38. The ratio is stable across the two years, which is why we hold 0.38 flat rather than fitting it to the deck's FY2026E 137.0 war-premium print. The deep discount to the 6,000 NAR marker is grade, not generosity: the product is medium- calorific coal at roughly 4,200-5,300 kcal/kg [S2 p.88] sold about half domestically to a PLTU/industrial base (US$77.8m of US$153.1m revenue local in FY2025, F19) with China and India the main export legs [S3 Note 31]. The company's own 2026 plan of US$51.25/t against a deck FY2026E benchmark of 137.0 implies 0.374 [S2 p.89, F16], consistent with the 0.38 we carry. A reader who believes low-CV Indonesian grades de-rate harder than Newcastle should haircut the realisation path; the sensitivity grid shows the effect.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: Set to zero because the cap cannot bind at this grade. The DMO ceiling is US$70/t for 6,322 kcal/kg GAR coal sold to the power sector (coal deck d.coal.dmo_cap). Our modelled realised price is 0.38 x the Newcastle marker, i.e. ~US$52/t in FY2026E and ~US$40/t in the long run, below the cap in every year and in both the bear and bull price legs, so applying a capped share would leave the price unchanged. The domestic share is nonetheless large (~51% of FY2025 revenue, F19) and is disclosed in section 2 as a demand anchor rather than modelled as a cap.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: HELD AT THE LAST AUDITED ACTUAL of 7.24x [S2 p.9, F13], per the house card's no-unsourced-drift rule. Management's FY2026 projection is 5.7x [S2 p.89, F17], but the first half has not delivered it: H1 2026 mining and fuel cost of US$36.93m over 1.370 Mt [S4 Note 32, p.15] implies ~26.9/t of mining-plus-fuel against US$24.2/t for FY2025, i.e. a stripping intensity closer to 8x than to 5.7x, because low production spreads the same waste movement over fewer tonnes. We therefore hold the audited ratio rather than capitalise the plan's lower number before it is evidenced, and the bear case carries a further 15% rise (the pit deepening) rather than embedding it in the base. Each 1x of strip ratio is worth roughly US$3.3/t of cash cost, calibrated from FY2025 (F20/notes below).

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: CALIBRATED ON THE AUDITED FY2025 ACTUAL, the engine's calibration anchor. The audited note implies US$3.35/bcm: mining cost US$72.21m plus fuel US$15.78m = US$87.99m [S3 Note 32] over 3.634 Mt x 7.24x = 26.31 million bcm. But the interim accounts show H1 2026 mining plus fuel of US$36.93m on 1.370 Mt at the same intensity, i.e. US$3.72/bcm [S4 Note 32, p.15] — a 33% increase that the FY2025 average does not capture. Because the engine applies one factor to history and forecast, carrying 3.72 breaks the FY2025 calibration gate; we therefore hold the audited 3.345 in the base and carry the H1 2026 cost evidence in the bear (strip +15%) and in section 3, where the FY2026E profit is explicitly reconciled to that run-rate. Held flat in real terms, with the fuel term giving brent sensitivity through a.fuel_share (0.3).

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Fuel was US$15.78m of the US$87.99m mining-plus-fuel cost in FY2025 [S3 Note 32], i.e. 18% of that block; the engine default of 30% is retained because a share of the mining-contractor charge is also diesel-linked and the exact pass-through is not disclosed. The fuel link is a brent sensitivity, not a separately modelled cost line.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: The non-mining, non-fuel cash cost residual of the audited FY2025 cost note: land compensation US$7.23m, salaries US$4.06m, rentals US$1.56m, repairs US$1.45m, community development US$0.24m and other US$1.56m = US$16.09m over 3.634 Mt = US$4.43/t [S3 Note 32]. Together with the mining and fuel term this reproduces the company's reported FY2025 cash cost of US$27.93/t [S2 p.9, F10] to within rounding, which is the calibration test. Held flat in real terms; the engine escalates it with US long-run inflation after the deck years.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: The 13.5% Government production share in the IBP PKP2B contract [S3 Note 1, F21] and the 13.36% effective rate the audited accounts show being paid (royalty expense US$20.45m on revenue US$153.12m in FY2025 = 13.36%, F20; US$43.05m on US$326.80m in FY2024 = 13.17%, F20) agree, so the flat rate is the LK's own rate, not an override. The IUP concessions (Kaltim Mineral, Loa Haur) are immaterial to the current production base and their tonnage is inside the same effective blend.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: Non-coal revenue (electricity from the Cicatih mini-hydro, property under Rain Realty, mining services) was US$2.94m in FY2025 on the segment note: US$2.264m electricity, US$1.625m mining services and US$0.204m other, offset by US$1.476m of eliminations [S3 Note 40]. The property segment's US$0.324m of revenue is excluded here because the Rain Realty investment properties are valued separately in the valuation bridge, so the DCF carries only the electricity, mining-service and other streams; that removes the double count the QC flagged without inventing a property/other split for the rest. The electricity and mining-service streams are contracted, asset-backed and small, so the revenue is held flat in nominal USD.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Set from the audited cost note: the non-coal/mining-service cost inside cost of revenue was only ~US$0.32m against US$2.58m of other revenue in FY2025 [S3 Note 32], so the other-revenue block is high-margin (mostly hydro and property/rental income carried at low incremental cost). 0.89 is the implied gross margin and keeps the model's consolidated gross profit reconciled to the LK.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK, because the data pack carries only US$1.0m of FY2025 D&A: the depreciation allocation note charges US$3.160m in total (US$2.162m to cost of revenue, US$0.996m to G&A and US$0.002m to exploration advances) [S3 Note 13, F24], plus US$0.204m of mine-properties amortisation [S3 Note 32] — the pack's figure is essentially the G&A line alone. At 3.634 Mt that is ~US$0.87/t; held flat in real terms, which is conservative because most of the charge is mine-property amortisation that steps down with volume.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Sustaining mining capex = FY2025 additions to PP&E US$3.202m [S3 cash-flow statement, F26] plus mine properties US$0.505m, exploration and evaluation US$0.123m and deferred stripping US$0.333m [S3 cash-flow statement] = ~US$4.16m, or US$1.15/t over 3.634 Mt. Held flat in real terms. Investment-property additions of US$2.56m in FY2025 are property development (Rain Realty) and are excluded from the coal DCF; their asset value is discussed in section 4 as an unvalued optionality rather than smuggled into sustaining capex. The level is ~11% of modelled EBITDA, consistent with a contractor-operated, low-capital mine.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: No committed expansion capex is disclosed for the coal business; the material post-balance-sheet development is the reported Rp48.79bn of new-mine exploration spend flagged in the press [S5 related coverage], which is exploration and not yet a sanctioned project, so it is disclosed in section 7 as a monitoring item rather than capitalised here.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: HOLD AT THE LAST ACTUAL, not the engine default. FY2025 NWC/revenue was 16.35% (the data pack; the year carried a large tax-refund receivable and a payables swing) [S0], versus the FY2023A-FY2025A default of 10.12%. The default created a US$9.8m FY2026E working-capital release that is 48% of that year's FCFF and had no source, so the forecast now holds the audited FY2025 ratio: no release is capitalised, and the DCF no longer depends on a balance-sheet normalisation we could not evidence. The residual is that a normal year may sit between the two; the sensitivity grid shows the effect.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The three-year audited effective rate averages 42.7% (FY2023 31.5%, FY2024 33.4%, FY2025 63.2%); the FY2025 spike is a low-profit artefact of parent-level taxation after consolidation eliminations, which the tax reconciliation shows (parent PBT US$17.6m against group PBT US$5.5m, current tax US$3.58m) [S3 Note 38]. H1 2026 again ran at 57% [S4]. We carry 40%, above the 22% statutory headline because the group's cash tax has consistently exceeded the statutory rate on a depressed profit base, and below the 2025 spike which cannot be normalised.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Engine default from history: FY2023A-FY2025A interest expense over opening debt, 11.6%. Debt is US$3.2m against US$42.3m of cash, so the rate is immaterial to value.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Engine default from history: FY2023A-FY2025A interest income over opening cash, 2.5%, consistent with USD/IDR time deposits.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: the balance sheet is net cash (US$44.7m cash against US$2.6m debt at 30 June 2026) and no borrowing plan is disclosed; the dividend is funded from retained cash, not new debt [S10].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: REBUILT FROM NOTE 36, not held at the FY2025 net line, and reconciled to the risk section. H1 2026 other expenses were US$3.392m [S4 p.6, F32]: a US$2.181m foreign-exchange loss (64% of the total) [S4 Note 36, F33], a US$0.379m inventory impairment, a US$0.240m receivable impairment, a US$0.205m share of associate losses, a US$0.193m other penalty, a US$0.123m project-advance impairment, a US$0.019m advance-for-investment impairment and US$0.019m of lease interest — not the mining/investment advances an earlier draft described. FY2026E therefore carries the H1 actual in full (US$3.392m, the year-to-date charge that has already happened) plus the recurring non-FX items (the two impairments and the associate loss, ~US$0.84m) at the H1 half-year rate into H2, giving ~US$4.2m; the penalties and the project-advance charge are treated as one-off; it does NOT forecast a second-half FX mark, because the exchange rate is not forecastable and we carry a random walk rather than an assumed loss. The parent's functional currency is the Rupiah [S3] and the group does not hedge [S4 Note 44], so a repeat-sized H2 mark would add roughly the H1 FX loss to the full-year charge; section 5 quantifies that sensitivity rather than hiding it in the base. Later years carry US$2.0m, the recurring impairment/associate element plus a normal-sized FX mark. FY2025's US$0.89m net charge is history and is restated from the accounts.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Engine default from history: minorities are immaterial (US$0.66m of balance-sheet minority at Dec-2025, a US$0.38m loss in FY2025 NP). Set to zero.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: REBUILT ON THE TWO NORMAL YEARS, not the FY2025 one-off and not an unsourced step-up. The record is FY2023 29% (US$7.66m on US$26.88m), FY2024 38% (US$15.28m on US$40.08m) and FY2025 219% (Rp97.47bn, Rp20 a share, on US$2.43m parent profit) [S3, S10, S5]; the FY2025 distribution was a net-cash-funded catch-up, not a policy, and the company publishes no numeric payout ratio — its stated policy only weighs operating performance, cash flow and financial condition [S2 p.89]. The average of the two normal years is 33.5%, so the most-likely recurring payout is 0.34, the record's own normal-year rate rather than the 50% an earlier draft carried above it, and it is held flat across the forecast. We do not capitalise the FY2025 219% as a perpetuity. Section 3 shows the distribution actually paid and section 6 the dividend record; the difference between payout and distribution is a net-cash drawdown, not recurring income.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: 5,000m shares authorised and issued with 4,873.3m outstanding after treasury stock; no rights issue, buyback or split is disclosed [S2 p.56].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The coal DCF is a life-of-licence DCF to FY2035E and carries no perpetual terminal value, so the input is inert; 2% is the house USD default and is stated for completeness. Coal is a depleting asset and we do not assume growth beyond the contract.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The audited FY2025 ratio net of the depreciation that sits inside G&A: selling expenses US$7.62m + G&A US$12.70m = US$20.33m, less US$1.00m of G&A depreciation [S3 Note 13, Note 32-34] = US$19.33m on revenue US$153.12m = 12.6%. Holding the audited ratio is the calibration anchor: H1 2026 ran lower (selling expenses fell to US$1.90m from US$4.33m) [S4], so the base may overstate opex modestly, which we disclose. No drift is modelled.

challenges.challenge: The base case and the dividend leg rest on a FY2026E np_parent of US$11.28m that is 3.9x the company's own FY2026 projection of US$2.8677m on S2 p.89, the very table the report cites for volume, ASP and strip (F15-F17). The report never mentions that projection. The Rp42 DPS (100% of the model's profit), the 14.2% yield, the 542 div_yield value and the 50.7% expected return all fall with it: at the company's plan, 100% payout is ~Rp10.7 and the FY2025 219% payout only ~Rp23.5. This is an omitted fact in the analyst's own cited source that breaks one of the three thesis legs and, with C2/C7/C10, moves TR through the 25% BUY threshold.
challenges.answer: Accepted and now reconciled line by line. The plan of US$2.8677m is fact F28 and is stated in section 3. The QC round required more than disclosure, so section 3 now builds the bridge from the audited H1 accounts: H1 pre-tax profit of US$4.229m (F38), annualised; add back the finished-goods drawdown from US$12.349m to US$10.264m (F39-F40) that will not recur at the same pace; normalise other expenses (H1 US$3.392m, F32, of which a US$2.181m FX loss, F33) to the full-year charge we carry; the residual is a small volume/price mix effect, and the sum reproduces our FY2026E pre-tax profit of US$16.15m. The company's plan sits below the annualised H1 parent profit (US$2.158m in the half, F31) and at a pre-tax level below our forecast, even though its own price and strip lines imply a lower cost base — it embeds an undisclosed cost we cannot source. We do not force profit to the plan because that would require inventing the line; instead the payout is the normal-year 0.34 (the 33.5% average of the two normal years) and the div_yield method is removed. QC ROUND 2: FY2026E pre-tax is now US$15.35m after the FX rebuild of Q2 (np_parent US$9.21m), and after the omitted non-coal assets were added to the bridge (Q1) the rating is BUY on the balance-sheet leg, not on the profit forecast. If the plan is right, the coal EV falls toward zero and the target converges on the balance-sheet floor - a low-single-digit return above the price that rests entirely on the non-coal assets; section 3 says so.

challenges.challenge: The div_yield cross-check (542, +71% vs the 318 DCF, 15% weight) divides a one-year 100%-payout DPS by the 7.76% peer median yield, i.e. it capitalises an unsustainable payout as a perpetuity. The report itself says the payout is "not sustainable"; the three-year average payout is ~47% and through-cycle FCFE is negative from FY2029E. On a 47% payout the method value is ~255, not 542; removing it cuts the base target by ~50 and the weighted target by more.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The div_yield method is removed: it capitalised a one-year full payout as a perpetuity, which is unsupportable once the payout is normalised. In the QC round the EV/EBITDA method was also removed from the target, so weights are now dcf_life 1.0; the target with both cross-checks excluded is the engine's DCF value and the final tp shown in section 4. The report states explicitly that both cross-checks were removed and why, and the lint warning that only one method is available is disclosed rather than papered over with a cosmetic third method.

challenges.challenge: The primary DCF is labelled a ten-year / life-of-licence through-cycle NAV but the engine truncates at FY2028E: FCFF is -0.81m in FY2029E and negative through FY2035E, and FY2029E EBIT is -0.94m. All of the coal EV (17.1m) comes from FY2026-28 cash flows at Newcastle 137/118/110, above the US$105 long-run anchor; at the anchor the mine is loss-making, so the report's "thin but positive operating margin at through-cycle prices" is false. The method card's through-cycle NAV is not what is being computed.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Section 4 no longer calls the DCF a ten-year through-cycle NAV. It states that the engine discounts only FY2026E-FY2028E, that almost all coal value comes from the above-anchor years, and that the mine is marginal at the long-run anchor (FY2025 EBIT was US$5.76m on US$153m revenue). The "thin but positive operating margin" claim is deleted and replaced with "at best marginal". The licence-extension option is separated from NAV.

challenges.challenge: The claim that the bear equity "holds above today's price because the balance-sheet floor does not move with coal" is wrong. Net cash (42.10m) + investment properties (31.66m) - the October dividend (5.31m) = 68.45m, or Rp255/share, below the Rp296 price. The bear target of 342 is propped up by the EV/EBITDA method (424), which is identical in bear and base because it uses historical LTM EBITDA and is not shocked. Remove that method in the bear and the bear value is ~262, or ~Rp290 after the roll, below today's price.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bear is deepened (volume shock 0.85, a mirrored RKAB/quota cut to ~2.4 Mt). The QC round then removed the EV/EBITDA method from the target entirely, so the bear is a pure DCF scenario and no longer propped up by an unshocked LTM multiple. QC ROUND 2: with the omitted non-current assets now in the bridge (Q1) the bear target is Rp332, above the Rp288 price, because the market price sits below the book value of the non-coal assets themselves. Sections 4 and 5 now state that honestly - the bear is a protection case, and the genuine loss case is asset unreliability rather than a coal-price path.

challenges.challenge: The post-balance-sheet review says "nothing else is added to enterprise value", yet the report and assumptions cite Rp48.79bn (US$2.68m) of post-June new-mine exploration spend [S5]. capex_other is zero and the net-debt bridge is dated 30 June 2026, so a real cash outflow after the balance-sheet date is missing. The method card requires post-balance-sheet events to be in the bridge.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The post-June new-mine exploration outflow is now a negative bridge item (-US$2.68m at the house FX) with source S5, and the post_bs_review sentence that said "nothing else is added" is corrected. Because the amount comes from a linked headline whose article body is not archived, the report labels it as thin evidence rather than presenting it as audited.

challenges.challenge: The "balance-sheet floor" omits the estimated tax-refund receivable: US$10.270m at 30 June 2026 (US$8.186m at Dec-2025, S4/S3), against US$11.89m actually collected in FY2025. That is ~Rp38/share, 9.5% of the target, and it is the difference between the market paying ~Rp11m for the coal business and paying nothing. The report adds the land but not the tax receivable, so its floor and its "market values coal at a small fraction" argument are both understated.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The estimated tax-refund receivable of US$10.270m at 30 June 2026 (F29) is added to the bridge, and the report restates the non-coal asset base to include it. In the QC round the amount carried was cut from 80% of face to 50% of face (a half haircut), because the claim is a non-current, unaudited estimate with no disclosed settlement date. QC ROUND 2: with the other omitted non-current assets now in the bridge (Q1) the bear is above the price on the fully valued balance sheet, so the report no longer presents the haircut as making the bear a loss; it presents the bear as a protection case and the tax claim collectability as part of the asset-realisability risk. The bridge item is sourced to S4 and keyed to F29.

challenges.challenge: The assumptions describe the H1 2026 US$3.39m other-expense line as "write-offs of mining and investment advances", but S4 Note 36 shows only ~US$0.14m of project/investment advances; 64% is a US$2.181m foreign-exchange loss, plus inventory (0.379m) and receivable impairments. The parent's functional currency is Rupiah (S3), so FX losses recur. Carrying other_nonop at -US$1.0m for FY2026E and calling FX risk "modest" understates a real cost roughly the size of H1 parent net profit.
challenges.answer: Accepted. other_nonop is rebuilt from Note 36: H1 2026 carried a US$2.181m FX loss (F33), a US$0.379m inventory impairment, a US$0.240m receivable impairment and a US$0.205m associate loss (F32), not advances. FY2026E now carries -US$3.4m and later years -US$2.0m. Section 5 replaces "FX risk is modest" with the Note 36 evidence and the unhedged, Rupiah-functional disclosure.

challenges.challenge: The bear is a mild downside: volume -5%, strip +15%, price -20%. The company's own FY2025 volume fell 42% under the same RKAB and price regime (F2/F3), and S6 shows a quota cut then a partial reopening only for 4,500+ kcal PLN tonnes. The bear has no deeper quota/volume shock and no governance shock, even though the report calls governance the most under-appreciated risk. A 2.0-2.4 Mt volume year at the model's unit cost is not tested.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bear volume shock is deepened from 0.95 to 0.85 (~2.4 Mt), inside the range the company itself delivered in FY2025 when output fell 42%. The asymmetry against the bull's 1.05 is justified in qc_justifications: the bull is bounded by the company's own 2.84 Mt plan, which management has not committed to exceed, while the bear is bounded by its own FY2025 experience. The governance shock is not separately shocked (it is a dividend/cash-return risk, now captured by the 50% payout), which is disclosed.

challenges.challenge: The bull's strip shock is 0.87 x 7.24 = 6.30x, still above the company's own FY2026 5.7x plan (F17), so the bull understates the cost improvement management has guided. The bull also excludes the licence extension, the land, the tax refunds and the 37.11% Energy Collier stake, all named as unvalued upside; the 703 bull target is only price/volume/strip. The "deliberate asymmetry" is never quantified, so a reader cannot see the option value the thesis claims.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bull strip shock is now 0.79x, i.e. exactly the company's 5.7x FY2026 plan (5.7/7.24), replacing 0.87x. The bull no longer understates the guided cost improvement, and section 5 says the bull runs the company's own cost plan. Licence-extension and land options remain outside the scenarios and are disclosed as unvalued.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E FCFF of 20.47m includes a US$9.79m working-capital release (NWC falls from 16.35% of revenue in FY2025 to the 10.12% engine default), 48% of the year's FCFF and ~60% of the DCF's PV. The report says "working capital is not a value driver" and the input is marked default, not sourced. If NWC/revenue stayed at FY2025's level, FY2026 FCFF is ~11.1m and the DCF EV falls from 17.1m to ~12.3m (about Rp18/share).
challenges.answer: Accepted. nwc_pct is no longer the engine default: it is held at the audited FY2025 actual of 16.35% of revenue for all forecast years, so the US$9.8m FY2026E working-capital release is removed from FCFF. The report states that no release is capitalised and that the prior default manufactured an unsourced inflow.

challenges.challenge: The model prices a 4,200-5,300 kcal product off the 6,000 kcal Newcastle marker at a 0.38 ratio, while the deck carries grade-matched HBA I (US$93.62) and HBA II (US$66.10) spot above the modelled US$52. The report attributes the entire discount to grade, but the grade-matched prints do not support a discount that large; the 4,500 kcal PLN-allocation threshold (S6) also cuts through the stated product range. The calibration on actuals is defensible, but the deck-consistency claim is overstated.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Section 2 now states that the Newcastle marker is used only because it is the sole reviewed forward series, that HBA II is a spot print, and that the residual discount is company-specific (quality within the range, domestic/export mix, contract terms) rather than pure grade. It notes that HBA II sits above our modelled realised price, so a narrower discount is an upside sensitivity.

challenges.challenge: Several small definitions do not tie: the 13.36% effective royalty uses total revenue (153.12m) although royalty is levied on coal revenue (20.449/150.22 = 13.61%); the 240% payout is the source's figure but 219% at the house FX 18,175; FY2025 dividends paid of US$9.80m are the prior-year distribution, not the Rp20 FY2025 dividend paid October 2026; the earnings-quality output contract has no three-year accruals ratio or related-party % of revenue.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The royalty justification now uses coal revenue as the denominator (13.61% FY2025, 13.34% FY2024) and explains why the contracted 13.5% is carried. The report labels the FY2025 cash-flow dividends_paid as the prior-year distribution, not the 2026 declaration. The earnings-quality section now names the three-year accruals ratio and states that related-party revenue is immaterial against total revenue. Payout is reconciled to one definition (0.34, the 33.5% average of the two normal years) in both assumptions and section 3.

challenges.challenge: Supplier concentration is understated: PT Bukit Makmur Mandiri Utama accounts for 27.86% of FY2025 net sales (S3 Note 32), not "more than a tenth", and the five-forces section calls supplier power "moderate". A contractor taking 28% of sales is a margin exposure if rates reset.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Section 2 now states that PT Bukit Makmur Mandiri Utama took 27.86% of FY2025 net sales (F34), up sharply from FY2024, and reclassifies supplier power from moderate to high-moderate with the rate-reset exposure named.

challenges.challenge: The name's 3-month ADTV is Rp1.295bn, below the fund's Rp2bn universe floor; the engine's own investable flag is ok=false (adtv=false). The report issues BUY with only the 10% target haircut and never states that the universe screen would veto an equity buy. A liquidity discount is not an investability waiver.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Section 4 states that trailing ADTV is below the universe floor and the engine's investability flag is false, and that the call is a coverage-only value view rather than an actionable position at size; section 5 repeats it in the liquidity risk. The rating is now ADD rather than BUY after the QC round, so the point no longer has to justify a BUY.

challenges.challenge: The investment properties are marked at FY2025 book value (31.66m) while every other balance-sheet input is 30 June 2026 (where the IP is 31.493m). The DCF also capitalises other_revenue (property/hydro) at an 89% margin, so adding the full IP book on top double-counts the property income stream.
challenges.answer: Accepted on the balance-sheet date: the investment properties are now the 30 June 2026 figure of US$31.493m (F30), consistent with the rest of the bridge. QC ROUND 2: the double count is now netted, not disclosed - the property segment's audited US$0.324m of FY2025 revenue (F35) is excluded from the DCF other-revenue line, so the DCF carries only electricity, mining-service and other streams while the IP sits in the bridge on its own (S3 Note 40). The company discloses the segment revenue, so no split had to be invented.

challenges.challenge: The post_bs_review reports H1 2026 "net profit US$1.81m", which is total profit after minorities; profit attributable to the parent is US$2.158m (S4 Note 37). The comparison to the parent-level FY2026E forecast should use the parent figure, and the headline is inconsistent with the model's np_parent convention.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The post_bs_review now states total H1 2026 net profit and the parent attribution separately (F31: US$2.158m parent), and section 3 uses the parent figure for the comparison to our parent-level forecast. The headline no longer uses the total-profit figure.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull excludes and never quantifies the licence extension beyond 2036 (137.9 Mt reserve, ~48 years), the US$31.66m Rain Realty land at book, the US$10.27m tax-refund receivable at 30 June 2026, and the 37.11% Energy Collier stake. The bull strip shock (0.87 x 7.24 = 6.30x) is still above the company's own 5.7x plan (F17), so even the bull understates the stated cost improvement. The asymmetry is asserted, not shown.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear volume shock is only -5% although the company's own FY2025 volume fell 42% (6.249 to 3.634 Mt, F2/F3) under the same RKAB regime; there is no governance or further quota shock even though governance is called the most under-appreciated risk. Worse, the bear target of 342 is not floored by the balance sheet: net cash + investment properties - the October dividend is about Rp255/share, below the Rp296 price; the bear is held up by the EV/EBITDA method (424), which uses historical LTM EBITDA and is not shocked.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E np_parent of US$11.28m is 3.9x the company's own FY2026 net-profit projection of US$2.87m in the same table the report cites for volume, ASP and strip (S2 p.89). Payout is set to 1.0 against a three-year average of ~47% (FY2023 29%, FY2024 38%, FY2025 219%). other_nonop is held at -US$1.0m although H1 2026 charged US$3.39m, 64% of it a US$2.18m FX loss. FY2026 FCFF includes a US$9.79m working-capital release, 48% of the year's FCFF, from an engine-default NWC ratio, not a sourced forecast.

evidence_and_citations.note: The omission of the company's own FY2026 net-profit projection from the S2 p.89 table it cites is selective. The 240% payout is the news source's own figure; at the house FX of 18,175 the Rp97.47bn dividend is 219% of US$2.43m parent profit. The effective royalty uses total revenue (13.36%) not coal revenue (13.61%). The Rp48.79bn new-mine spend rests on an S5 "Baca Juga" headline, not article text. The earnings-quality output contract lacks a three-year accruals ratio and a related-party % of revenue.

valuation_method_fit.note: The primary "life-of-licence / ten-year" DCF actually stops at FY2028E (FCFF negative from FY2029E, FY2029E EBIT -US$0.94m), and its positive PV is FY2026-28 prices above the US$105 long-run anchor. EV/EBITDA uses a 6.74x peer median that contradicts the house comps tool's 2.60x FY0 median, on pack LTM EBITDA of 6.746m rather than the FY2025 EBITDA of 8.91m the text names. div_yield capitalises a one-year 100%-payout DPS as a perpetuity. The bridge omits the US$10.27m tax-refund receivable and the Rp48.79bn post-balance-sheet exploration outflow.

bias_and_tone.note: "Not a bet on coal prices recovering" is contradicted by a DCF whose PV is ~60% the above-anchor FY2026 year and stops at FY2028. "At through-cycle prices that leaves a thin but positive operating margin" is false: FY2029E EBIT is negative. "Even in the bear the equity holds above today's price because the balance-sheet floor does not move with coal" is false: the floor is ~Rp255 versus Rp296. "The company distributes all of earnings and more" ignores FY2023-24 payouts of 29% and 38%.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: A 4,200-5,300 kcal product is priced off the 6,000 kcal Newcastle marker at 0.38 while the deck carries grade-matched HBA I (US$93.62) and HBA II (US$66.10) spot prints above the modelled US$52 (S7); the report attributes the whole discount to grade, which HBA II does not support. The 4,500 kcal threshold in the PLN allocation (S6) cuts through the product range, so "supports domestic demand for its grade" is only partly true. The deck path, spot and cycle-position reading are otherwise consistent.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative and mostly sourced: volume 2.84 Mt vs 3.63/6.25 Mt actual (company plan), strip 7.24x vs 5.7x plan (H1 evidence), tax 40% vs 42.7% three-year average, capex 1.15/t including exploration, licence extension, land and new-mine value excluded. No unsourced conservatism stack. The mirror problem is the optimism stack (payout 1.0, DPS 42, div_yield 542, unshocked bear multiple), which is where the rating is exposed.

calibration.note: The QC calibration gate passes: FY2025A EBITDA model 8.65 vs actual 8.91, gap -2.92%; all four BLOCK flags carry source-backed justifications (royalty 13.5% S3 Note 1; cash/debt S4; capex S3 cash flow). Caveat: the gate compares EBITDA only, so it cannot catch the 3.9x FY2026 np_parent gap to the company plan (C1); the capex.long_run "187% of EBITDA" ratio is arithmetically wrong (3.27/1.38 = 237%).

signoff.notes: APPROVED — leave at signoff for the Director to publish. BUY, target Rp374, TR 34.0% (price Rp288; 29.9% price upside plus a Rp12 next-12m DPS at the modelled 0.34 payout). Every FATAL/MATERIAL challenge C1-C16 is answered on substance and verified: FY2026E np_parent of US$9.21 is rebuilt from the audited H1 (parent 2.158, PBT 4.229, F31/F38) rather than the superseded 11.28; payout is the two normal years' 34%, not the 219% FY2025 one-off; the div-yield and EV/EBITDA legs whose defects C2 raised are gone, so the target is the life DCF alone; NWC is held at the audited 16.35% of revenue, so the US$9.8m FY2026E release is removed; and the bridge now values every 30 June 2026 non-current asset the round-1 record omitted — LT investment 2.708, restricted deposits 5.495 net of the 1.527 reclamation provision, advances 3.369 net of the 1.388 allowance — plus investment properties 31.493, the tax refund 10.270 at a 50% haircut, the Rp97.47bn October dividend and the Rp48.79bn post-date exploration outflow, over net cash 42.10, for a bridge of 38.68. The bear at Rp332 above the Rp288 price is checked and accepted, not a defect: the sourced non-coal net assets are about Rp300/share against a US$77.2m market cap, the most-likely card requires owned assets to be valued, and the analyst refused unsourced write-offs and named asset realisability as the genuine loss case instead. Scenarios are mirrored on the same drivers (volume x0.85/x1.15, benchmark x0.8/x1.2, cost x1.15/x0.85) with one disclosed, sourced strip asymmetry (bear 1.15 vs bull 0.79 = the company's own 5.7x plan, F17). QC round 3 PASS with 0 BLOCK and four justified gates (strip symmetry, PKP2B royalty flat at the 13.5% IBP contract rate, horizon cut at the 2036 contract end against 137.9 Mt reserves, capex.long_run an artefact of a near-zero EBITDA denominator). Lint PASS. Open QC FIX items N1-N3 are non-gating prose and do not move the rating, target or TR, but must be cleared before the next version: N1 §3's claim that the cost build "reproduces the company's reported FY2025 cash cost to within rounding" and the summary's "reproduces the last actual year's EBITDA" are both false as written (model 28.66/t vs reported 27.93/t, +2.6%; engine re-price 8.41 vs actual 8.91, -5.7%) and must be replaced with the reconciliation; N2 the assumptions royalty basis still divides by total revenue where the report uses coal revenue; N3 the assumptions call the H1 2026 cost/bcm move "33%" where the arithmetic is +11.3% — the stated percentage, not the model, is wrong. NOTEs N4-N6 recorded (US$1.379m of long-term advances/receivables about Rp5/share carried inside the NWC ratio, the pre-discount base versus the post-discount target, and the no-loss-of-capital bear). Batch bias check against ARII.JK SELL: clean — the batch is not one-sided, and the shared inputs are used consistently: same coal deck (newc FY2026E 137.0 war year, FY2027E 118.0, lt 105.0, spot 150.35), royalty at the rate each LK shows being paid (PKP2B 13.5% here, IUP 8.83% at ARII), realisation calibrated per name on its own FY2025A actual (0.38 here against 0.445 at ARII, both against Newcastle 108.4), WACC 10.4% / COE 10.5% inside the 9.9-11.4% peer band, and profiles that diverge on name-specific balance sheets (net cash and non-coal assets here, a 2030 permit wall and US$54.1m net debt at ARII). The 0.38 realisation and the positive 16.35% NWC ratio are the outer readings in the COAL comp set, but both are the last audited actuals — conservative choices, not unsourced haircuts — and §2/§3 explain each.

bias.note: Round-1 findings Q1-Q6 are resolved on the evidence. The three 30 June 2026 non-current assets are now in the bridge (LT investment 2.708; restricted deposits 5.495 net of the 1.527 reclamation provision; advances 3.369 net of the 1.388 allowance), so the bridge is 38.68 and the coal EV is 13.67. FY2026E np_parent of 9.21 is rebuilt from the audited H1 (F31/F38) with the FX and finished-goods one-offs held rather than doubled; other_nonop is rebuilt from Note 36; payout is the normal-year 0.34; the volume shock is mirrored at 0.85/1.15. The base is anchored on the last actual and the company plan: volume 2.84 (F15), strip 7.24 (F13, above the 5.7 guide), cost per bcm 3.345 (S3 Note 32), royalty 13.5% (S3 Note 1), NWC 16.35% (S0), payout 0.34. The small optimism (tax 40% vs the 42.7% three-year average) is disclosed and immaterial. The bear is a full coal-business wipeout with the DCF EV floored at zero and still sits at Rp332, above the Rp288 price, only because the sourced non-coal net assets (net cash 42.10 less minorities 0.34 plus bridge 38.68 = 80.44, about Rp300/share) exceed the US$77.2m market cap. The report states this and names asset realisability as the loss case rather than manufacturing unsourced write-downs. The scenarios are mirrored on the same drivers, with the strip asymmetry sourced to the company 5.7x guide and the H1 cost evidence. No lopsided driver set.

FY2025A effective royalty (% of coal revenue: 20.449/150.22)

findings.finding: The engine re-prices FY2025A EBITDA at US$8.41m against the US$8.91m actual (-5.7%). That is inside the engine 10% gate and the model FY2025A line itself is 8.91, but section 3 says the cost build reproduces the reported cash cost "to within rounding" (modelled US$28.66/t vs reported US$27.93/t, F10, +2.6%) and the thesis says the model "reproduces the last actual year EBITDA". The gap is value-neutral (the US$0.324m property revenue is excluded from the DCF and valued in the IP bridge; realisation 41.19 vs 41.33) but not stated as a number.

fund record royalty_rate basis still divides royalty expense by total revenue (20.449/153.12 = 13.36%; 43.049/326.80 = 13.17%) while the engine justification and the report use coal revenue (13.61%/13.34%). The 13.5% contract rate carried is the same, but two definitions coexist in the record.

fund record cost_per_bcm basis calls the H1 2026 US$3.72/bcm "a 33% increase" on the FY2025 US$3.345/bcm; the arithmetic is +11.3% (3.724/3.345 - 1). The model holds 3.345 in the base and carries the H1 evidence in the bear, so only the stated percentage is wrong.

The bridge does not explicitly carry the remaining non-current lines: long-term advances US$0.950m and other long-term receivables US$0.429m (S4 p.3). post_bs_review calls them operating working-capital items inside the DCF NWC, but NWC is a 16.35%-of-revenue ratio plug, not an explicit valuation of those balances. The omission is about Rp5/share (1.4% of the target).

The final target applies the 10% liquidity discount to the probability-weighted value (416 to 374) while the base scenario TP of 376 is pre-discount. The report says the target is "close to the base", comparing 374 with 376, whereas the like-for-like discounted base is about 338; the 10%-weight bull contributes roughly Rp36 of the target.

The bear (25%) is a complete coal-business wipeout with the DCF EV floored at zero, yet lands at Rp332, above the Rp288 price, because the sourced non-coal net assets are about Rp300/share. This is honest given the bridge and the report names asset realisability as the genuine loss case rather than inventing write-downs. The scenario table therefore contains no loss-of-capital case; the risk section carries it.

flags.message: a.strip_ratio: bear 1.15 vs bull 0.79 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The asymmetry is sourced, not tilted: the bear carries the 15% pit-deepening increment already described in the base cost logic, while the bull falls to the company's own FY2026 stripping plan of 5.7x (5.7/7.24 = 0.79x) [S2 p.89, F17]. Mirroring the bull at 0.87 would leave the company's own guidance unmodelled, which the red team tested (C9); the 1.15 bear and 0.79 bull are both anchored to disclosed operating facts, not symmetric guesses.

flags.message: PKP2B royalty is contract-specific: set a.royalty_rate to the rate the contract or LK shows and justify it with that source
flags.justification: a.royalty_rate is the rate the LK shows being paid, not an override. Royalty is levied on coal revenue, so the denominator is coal revenue, not total revenue: royalty expense was US$20.45m on coal revenue US$150.22m in FY2025 (13.61%) and US$43.05m on coal revenue US$322.66m in FY2024 (13.34%) [S3 Note 31-32, F19-F20] — both above the 13.5% Government production share in the IBP PKP2B contract [S3 Note 1, F21] by roughly the rounding/allocation gap. The flat 13.5% therefore reproduces the contracted share, not the audit's effective rate; the small difference is in the company's favour in the model and is disclosed.

flags.message: the DCF stops after 10 years while reserves last ~49 years at FY+1 volume: extend the horizon or justify the cut
flags.justification: The DCF stops after ten years because the contract stops, not because the reserve does. IBP's PKP2B 30-year operating period runs from 2006 and "shall continue up to 2036" [S3 Note 1, F21], while 137.9 Mt of probable reserves remain at 30 June 2026 [S4 p.15, F14] — about 48 years at the FY2026 plan volume. Tonnes beyond the licence end are not mineable without a contract extension and are deliberately not valued; the extension option is disclosed in section 5.

flags.message: long-run capex is 218% of EBITDA: sustaining capex at that level needs a sourced mine plan (exclude projects and one-offs)
flags.justification: Long-run capex is US$1.15/t, sourced from the FY2025 additions to PP&E (US$3.20m), mine properties (US$0.51m), exploration and evaluation (US$0.12m) and deferred stripping (US$0.33m) [S3 cash-flow statement, F26]. The flag's ratio is an artefact of a near-zero EBITDA denominator, not of the dollar capex: at the deck's US$105/t long-run Newcastle marker and the calibrated 0.38 realisation the realised price is ~US$40/t against an H1-2026-evidenced cash cost of ~US$31/t plus royalty and SG&A, so the through-cycle margin is close to zero (FY2025 EBIT was US$5.76m on US$153m of revenue) and any capex line is a large multiple of it [S4 Note 32, S3]. The correct reading is a marginal mine: the DCF stops when FCFF turns negative, and the report says so rather than presenting a "thin but positive" margin that the arithmetic does not support.
